httpRequests.name: 01 · Find your services
httpRequests.description:
Choose two supported services in the same workspace and region. Set serviceAId and serviceBId. Preserve their existing build configuration for recovery.

List services matching the provided filters. If no filters are provided, returns all services you have permissions to view.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/list-services

httpRequests.name: 02A · Inspect service A
httpRequests.description:
Confirm region, runtime, start command, runtime environment, and auto-deploy settings before linking.

Retrieve the service with the provided ID.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/retrieve-service

httpRequests.name: 02B · Inspect service B
httpRequests.description:
Confirm region, runtime, start command, runtime environment, and auto-deploy settings before linking.

Retrieve the service with the provided ID.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/retrieve-service

httpRequests.name: 03 · Create a Git build source
httpRequests.description:
Edit runtime, region, repoUrl, branch, and buildCommand first. Copy response.id to buildSourceId. This example does not link services during creation.

Create a build source that can be linked to one or more
services in the same workspace.

Exactly one of `git` or `image` must be set:
- `git`: the build source is git-backed. The code is built in
   the requested `region` (defaults to `oregon`).
- `image`: the build source is image-backed. It points at an
  existing image in an external registry; no build is performed.

`envVars`, `secretFiles`, and `envGroupIds` set the build-time
environment and are only valid for `git` sources; the request fails
if any are provided with `image`.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/create-build-source

httpRequests.name: 04 · Check build-time environment
httpRequests.description:
Optional: configure required build variables, secret files, or environment groups using the reference folders before linking. Service runtime variables are separate.

List all environment variables for the build source with the provided ID.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/get-env-vars-for-build-source

httpRequests.name: 05A · Link service A
httpRequests.description:
Run only after inspecting this service. This minimal body retains an existing native start command. If missing, add serviceDetails.startCommand for this service; Docker sources reject a start command.

Update the service with the provided ID.

400 with `code: build_source_region_mismatch` if `buildSourceId` names a git-backed
Build Source in a different region than the service.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-service

Links an existing service and replaces its build configuration. Confirm matching workspace and region, compatible runtime, and an existing start command for native runtimes. Do not include other build settings.

httpRequests.name: 05B · Link service B
httpRequests.description:
Run only after inspecting this service. This minimal body retains an existing native start command. If missing, add serviceDetails.startCommand for this service; Docker sources reject a start command.

Update the service with the provided ID.

400 with `code: build_source_region_mismatch` if `buildSourceId` names a git-backed
Build Source in a different region than the service.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-service

Links an existing service and replaces its build configuration. Confirm matching workspace and region, compatible runtime, and an existing start command for native runtimes. Do not include other build settings.

httpRequests.name: 06 · Trigger the shared build
httpRequests.description:
Starts a new build even if one already exists. Copy response.id (not buildRun.id) to buildId. Linked services with auto-deploy enabled deploy the result.

Start a new build of the build source at the current HEAD of its
branch, even if an up-to-date build already exists. Services linked to
the build source with autodeploy enabled are deployed with the result.

Updating a build source or its build-time environment (env vars,
secret files, env groups) with the REST API does not build it. Call
this endpoint after those changes to build them.

Only `git` build sources can be built.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/trigger-build-source-build

httpRequests.name: 07 · Check build status
httpRequests.description:
Repeat manually until buildRun.status is succeeded. If failed or canceled, inspect the build logs in Render before continuing.

Retrieve a build of a build source, including its status.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/retrieve-build-source-build

httpRequests.name: 08A · Deploy shared build to A (optional)
httpRequests.description:
Only needed for manual deployment. Wait for the selected build to succeed. Both requests use the same buildId. Skip if auto-deploy already deployed it.

Trigger a deploy for the service with the provided ID.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/create-deploy

httpRequests.name: 09A · Inspect deploys for A
httpRequests.description:
Inspect the latest deploy status and check the service in Render.

List deploys matching the provided filters. If no filters are provided, all deploys for the service are returned.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/list-deploys

httpRequests.name: 08B · Deploy shared build to B (optional)
httpRequests.description:

Trigger a deploy for the service with the provided ID.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/create-deploy

httpRequests.name: POST · Create a build source
httpRequests.description:
Create a build source that can be linked to one or more
services in the same workspace.

Exactly one of `git` or `image` must be set:
- `git`: the build source is git-backed. The code is built in
   the requested `region` (defaults to `oregon`).
- `image`: the build source is image-backed. It points at an
  existing image in an external registry; no build is performed.

`envVars`, `secretFiles`, and `envGroupIds` set the build-time
environment and are only valid for `git` sources; the request fails
if any are provided with `image`.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/create-build-source

httpRequests.name: GET · List build sources
httpRequests.description:
List build sources matching the provided filters. If `ownerId` is
omitted, returns build sources across every workspace you can view.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/list-build-sources

httpRequests.name: GET · Retrieve a build source
httpRequests.description:
Retrieve a shared build source by ID


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/get-build-source

httpRequests.name: PATCH · Update a build source
httpRequests.description:
Update a shared build source. Each top-level field is a true patch,
unset fields are left unchanged.

Supplying `git` or `image` can change the build source's
underlying identity:
- `image` on a git-backed build source switches it to image-backed
- `git` on an image-backed build source switches it to git-backed
- `git` on a build source that's already git-backed is a pure
  patch onto the existing config


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-build-source

httpRequests.name: DELETE · Delete a build source
httpRequests.description:
Delete the build source with the provided ID.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/delete-build-source

Destructive: review the target before sending. A build source must have no linked services before deletion.

Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-env-vars-for-build-source

httpRequests.description:

httpRequests.name: GET · List secret files
httpRequests.description:

Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/list-secret-files-for-build-source

httpRequests.description:
Replace all secret files for a build source with the provided list of secret files.

**Any of the build source's existing secret files not included in this request will be deleted.**

This only applies to secret files set directly on the build source, not to secret files in a linked environment group.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-secret-files-for-build-source

Replaces the entire collection. Retrieve existing values first and include all entries you want to keep. Trigger a build afterward.

httpRequests.name: POST · Link environment group
httpRequests.description:
Link a particular environment group to a particular build source.

The build source will have access to the environment variables and secret files in the group at build time.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/link-env-group-to-build-source

httpRequests.name: DELETE · Unlink environment group
httpRequests.description:
Unlink a particular environment group from a particular build source.

The build source will lose access to the environment variables and secret files in the group.


Reference: https://api-docs.render.com/reference/unlink-env-group-from-build-source

Destructive: review the target before sending. A build source must have no linked services before deletion.
